cards.explanation: The LORD opens with these words: “I have loved you…” says the LORD. (Malachi 1:2) Before any burden gets unpacked, before any question gets asked, He says that first. Friends, if somebody opens with those words, you lean in and listen.

The answer is True. Israel answers with a question. The LORD says He has loved them, and they ask, “How have You loved us?” (Malachi 1:2) That's a real question from the people, right in the middle of the LORD's words. I think they wanted Him to show them.

The answer is Jacob. The LORD says, “Yet Jacob I have loved…” (Malachi 1:2) Jacob is the one God later renamed Israel (Genesis 35:10), so the LORD is talking to Jacob's own family line. When they ask how He has loved them, He answers with a question about two brothers: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” (Malachi 1:2)

The word is wasteland. The LORD says, “…I have made his mountains a wasteland and left his inheritance to the desert jackals.” (Malachi 1:3) Mountains that should be solid and lasting, and the jackals get the inheritance. Friends, that's a hard picture to look at.

The answer is that He will tear down what they build. The LORD of Hosts says, “They may build, but I will demolish.” (Malachi 1:4) Edom, the people who came from Esau (Genesis 36:8-9), has plans to rebuild, but the LORD says what He will do about them. Rebuilding is a lot of work, and I wouldn't want to hear that part.

The answer is False. The LORD says Edom will be called the Land of Wickedness and “…a people with whom the LORD is indignant forever.” (Malachi 1:4) Forever is a long way from a little while. That's what the text says, and I'll leave it right there.

The answer is that He is great even beyond Israel. The LORD says Israel will see this with their own eyes and say, “The LORD is great—even beyond the borders of Israel.” (Malachi 1:5) They won't just hear about it, they'll see it for themselves. Friends, that's a big sentence about a big God.
